ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the acute-angled triangle $ABC$, where $AB=AC$, the circle $\odot O$ with $BC$ as the diameter intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$ respectively. Lines $OD$, $OE$, and $DE$ are connected. $DE\parallel BC$. If the radius of $\odot O$ is $m$, and $\tan\angle ABC=2$, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ADOE$ (expressed in an algebraic expression involving $m$)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB=AC$ and $BO=OC$,\\
we have $AO\perp BC$,\\
thus $\tan\angle ABC=\frac{AO}{OC}=2$,\\
since $OB=m$,\\
it follows that $OA=2m$,\\
since $\tan\angle C=\frac{BE}{EC}=2$,\\
we find $EC=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}m$,\\
given $AB=AC=\sqrt{5}m$,\\
thus $AE=AC-EC=\sqrt{5}m-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}m=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}m$,\\
since $DE\parallel CB$,\\
it follows that $\frac{DE}{BC}=\frac{AE}{AC}$,\\
thus $\frac{DE}{2m}=\frac{\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}m}{\sqrt{5}m}$,\\
consequently, $DE=\frac{6}{5}m$,\\
since $AO\perp BC$ and $DE\parallel BC$,\\
it follows that $AO\perp DE$,\\
hence the area of quadrilateral $ADOE$ is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot AO\cdot DE=\frac{1}{2}\times 2m\times \frac{6}{5}m=\boxed{\frac{6}{5}m^2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an isosceles triangle ABC with vertex A above and base BC horizontal, with AB and AC as the two legs. Circle O has BC as its diameter, and center O is at the midpoint of BC. The circle intersects AB and AC at D and E respectively; OD, OE, and DE are connected in the figure, and DE is drawn as a horizontal line parallel to BC; AO is the vertical line from the vertex to the midpoint of the base. In right triangle BEC, tan∠C=BE/EC=2. Let EC=x, then BE=2x, and BC=√(x^2+(2x)^2)=√5x=2m, so EC=x=2m/√5=2√5m/5. Therefore AE=AC−EC=√5m−2√5m/5=3√5m/5. Also because DE∥BC, △ADE∼△ABC, so DE/BC=AE/AC=(3√5m/5)/(√5m)=3/5. Thus DE=(3/5)·2m=6m/5. Since AO⊥BC and DE∥BC, AO⊥DE. The two diagonals AO and DE of quadrilateral ADOE are perpendicular, and its area is 1/2·AO·DE=1/2·2m·6m/5=6m^2/5.
